_readme: THE EVENT BOOK, phase 1 (80 events: 30 hand-built, 50 from the pilot of 20 Nov 2026). Schema: lib/star/life/types.ts LifeEvent. Conditions: lib/star/life/cond.ts. Checked by tests/star/lifeEvents.mts (validate.ts). 15 come from docs/plans/living-world-sample-events-2026-11-20.json (minigames that need new art became skill checks), 15 are new in the same schema. Money is weeks of your own wage. Every brand and paper is invented.

events.title: "Can I borrow the motor?"
setup: Your phone lights up on the dash: {mate.name}.
{mate.short}: "Mate. Big favour. It's my mum's sixtieth Saturday night. Can I turn up in yours? I'll have it back Sunday, washed."

outcomes.text: It comes back Sunday, washed, with a full tank and a can of KIB on the seat.
Sunday night. A photo arrives first. The front wing is against a bollard. "I am so, so sorry."
"Yeah. No. Fair enough." He hangs up a bit quick.

choices.label: "I'll do better. I'll drive you there myself."

outcomes.text: You drop him at the door. His mum makes you stay for cake. There is a photo of you two on her fridge now.

callbacks.line: "Was going to ask you for a lift. Then I remembered the car."
In a tight chance he shoots instead of squaring it while his grudge is 20 or more.
"Mum still asks after you."

events.title: He wants to make it right
setup: {mate.short} is waiting by your table with an envelope.
"That's the repair. All of it. And I've told the gaffer it was me, before the papers make it you."

outcomes.text: Square. He looks relieved, and a bit small.
He does not know what to say. He will not forget it.

callbacks.line: He is the first to stand up for you in the dressing room.
"Still owe you for the car. Don't think I've forgotten."

events.title: "Don't say anything. Just listen."
events.speaker: agent
setup: {agent.name}: "Don't say anything. Just listen. A bigger club had a man at your last three. They'll come in the summer. I can let that be known, or I can keep it very quiet. Your call."

outcomes.text: By Thursday it is on every feed. The gaffer does not look at you in training.

choices.label: "Keep it quiet. I've a season to finish."

outcomes.text: "Your funeral." He means it kindly. Mostly.

choices.label: Hang up. Go and tell the gaffer yourself.

outcomes.text: He listens, nods once. "Nobody has ever told me first."
He takes your silence as a yes. It is in the papers by Friday.
He takes your silence as a no, and sounds hurt about it.

callbacks.line: "You like the papers. Read about the team in them on Saturday."
"You came to me first, once. I've not forgotten."
"Going to run this one past the gaffer too?"
His opening ask for you is 5% lower: "I work as hard as I'm trusted."

events.title: The man from the tabloid
events.speaker: hack
setup: {hack.name} of the {hack.outlet} steps across you in the mixed zone, phone up, recording.
"{you.short}. Not a shot on target. Are you worth the money?"

choices.label: "Not today I wasn't. That's on me."

outcomes.text: He lowers the phone a little. The piece runs under 'NO EXCUSES'. Fair.
"Nothing to say, then." He says it loudly, for the others.

choices.label: "Have you ever kicked a ball in your life?"

outcomes.text: The clip has two million views by breakfast. Your own fans love it. He does not.
He sighs. Nobody prints that. Your gaffer likes it, though.
It goes out as a promise. The fans screenshot it. Saturday had better go well.

callbacks.line: "Fair play for last time. Not many front up."
His match reports mark you half a point kinder for 10 weeks.
"Remember me? I remember you."

events.title: "Sources close to the dressing room"
setup: Your phone will not stop. {hack.outlet}: "{you.short} 'THINKS HE'S BIGGER THAN THE CLUB', say team-mates."
{if source}The quotes sound a lot like {source.short}.{/if}

outcomes.text: It burns for a week and goes out.

choices.label: Ring him. Offer the sit-down interview he wanted.

outcomes.text: An hour in a hotel bar. The follow-up piece is called 'The other side of {you.short}'.
You put the paper on {source.short}'s seat in the canteen. He does not deny it. The room goes quiet.

callbacks.line: He will not sit at your table since the canteen.
"Still got the tape of that sit-down. Best thing I wrote all year."

events.title: The lad on his own
setup: {kid.name}, {kid.age}, up from the academy, is eating on his own with his headphones in.
{mate.short} waves you over to the usual table.

outcomes.text: He takes one headphone out. Ten minutes later he is telling you about his nan's jollof. He watches where you sit every day after that.

choices.label: Shout him over to the lads' table.

outcomes.text: He comes. The lads rip his trainers apart for ten minutes. He is grinning by the end.
He pretends not to hear, goes red, and leaves his food.
Nobody notices. That is rather the point.

callbacks.line: "Day one, you sat with me. I don't forget that."
He runs the length of the pitch to you when he scores.
"The lads still go on about my trainers. Worth it."

events.title: A day at the races
setup: You and {mate.short} in the owners' bar. He has a tip from his cousin: number 7, 'Offside Trap', 12 to 1 in the fourth.
{if owns:horse}Your own {you.horse} runs in the fifth.{/if}

choices.label: Put a proper bet on his tip.

outcomes.text: It wins by a nose. He is on the table. You are both on the back pages, grinning.
Fifth of nine. The money is gone. He cannot look at you. "My cousin is dead to me."

choices.label: A fiver each way, for a laugh.

outcomes.text: A good day. Nothing happens, in the best way. He tells you he is thinking of leaving in the summer; you are the first to know.

choices.label: "Forget his cousin. Back mine in the fifth."

outcomes.text: {you.horse} by two lengths. {mate.short} had fifty on it.
Last. "Lovely looking animal, though," he says, tearing up his slip.

callbacks.line: "How's the donkey?"
"My cousin says sorry about the horse. He's not allowed tips any more."
"Offside Trap. Still got the slip in my wallet."
If he is sold: a goodbye text that names the day.

events.title: He wants your number
events.speaker: rival
setup: {rival.name}, the new signing, is stood at your peg holding the number {you.number} shirt.
"I've worn this since I was nine. The club said to ask you. So I'm asking." {kitman.short} is pretending to fold socks.

outcomes.text: He hangs it back up, slowly. "Okay. We'll see who's wearing it in May."

choices.label: Hand it over. "Numbers don't score goals."

outcomes.text: He did not expect that. The kit man raises an eyebrow. The fans who bought your shirt are not happy.
Bar, first go. He shakes your hand properly.
He hits it. You don't. A deal is a deal. The fans who bought your shirt are not happy.
You say nothing. He hangs the shirt back on your peg, slowly. "Right." {kitman.short} folds the same sock twice.

callbacks.line: "May. Like I said."
He taps the number on his back when he walks past.
He points at his own number, at you, on the bench.

events.title: Who wears it in May
events.speaker: rival
setup: Last day of the season. {rival.short} is at your peg again, the goals chart from the canteen wall in his hand.
{if outscored(rival)}You scored more. He knows it.{/if}{if !outscored(rival)}He scored more. Everybody knows it.{/if}

outcomes.text: "Keep the shirt. You earned it." He means it. Something between you settles.
He shakes it, then asks for the shirt again. In front of everyone.

choices.label: Pin the chart back on the wall. Upside down.

outcomes.text: The lads howl. He does not.

choices.label: Give him the shirt. "You won it."

outcomes.text: The kit man sews your new number on that night. The gaffer nods at you in the corridor.
You walk past him to the showers. Behind you, the chart goes in the bin.

callbacks.line: He still has the chart. He keeps it in his locker.
"Most lads would have found a way out of that bet. You didn't."

events.title: Dad's old club
setup: Dad rings. He never rings. "The Sunday side. The one I took you to when you were five. The council want the pitch money or they fold. I'm not asking. I'm just telling you."

choices.label: Pay it. Today. Say nothing publicly.

outcomes.text: He goes quiet for a long time. "Your mum'll cry when I tell her." They paint your name on the hut.

choices.label: Pay it, and bring the cameras.

outcomes.text: Lovely pictures. Dad stands at the back of every one.
"No. No, course." The club folds in the spring. He tells you in passing.

callbacks.line: "The kids at the Sunday side still talk about you."
The Sunday side's kids form your guard of honour.
"I'd ask, but I know how you are with money."

events.title: The wrong boots
setup: {mate.short} chucks you a prototype pair from his brand, Vanta. "Try them. One session. Nobody's watching." They feel unbelievable.
Somebody was watching. A photo is on a fan account by tea time. {agent.short} texts: "Your boot people have seen it. Tell me that's edited."

outcomes.text: "It had better not." A fine comes off your next payment.

choices.label: "They're better than yours. Match them or I walk."

outcomes.text: A day of silence. Then a new offer, fee up.
"Then walk." They pull the bonus they owed you. Vanta do not ring.
They believe you. His brand does not see the funny side, and neither does he when he finds out why.

callbacks.line: "Ask one of your sponsors."
"Last time you bluffed, it cost us both."

events.title: 2:14 a.m.
events.speaker: stranger
setup: A text from a number you do not know. A photo: you, at the roulette table, clock on the wall behind you. 2:14 a.m. Match on Saturday.
"Nice night? The {hack.outlet} would pay me well for this. You can pay me better."

outcomes.text: The photo never appears.
He takes the money and sells it anyway. Now there are two stories.

choices.label: Go to the gaffer before it breaks.

outcomes.text: He is furious for four minutes and useful for ten. The club puts out a line before the paper does.

choices.label: "Sell it. I was there. So what."

outcomes.text: Front page Friday. Two goals Saturday. Sunday's headline: 'WHAT A GAMBLE'.
Front page Friday. A stinker Saturday. They boo you off.
Nothing. Then nothing. Then Saturday's paper.
He never texts again. You check your phone forty times a day for a month.

callbacks.line: "Casino this week, is it? Don't."
The next one asks double: "I hear you pay."
"Going to the casino before every game now, are we?"

events.title: It's probably nothing
events.speaker: physio
setup: Your hamstring tightens in the warm-up. {physio.name} presses a thumb into it and watches your face.
"Play Saturday and it's probably fine. Probably. Sit out and it's definitely fine. {boss.short} will ask me. What do I tell him?"

choices.label: "Tell him the truth. I'll sit this one out."

outcomes.text: You watch from the stand. Monday it feels brand new.
It holds. Just.
Sixty-third minute. You know before you hit the ground. Weeks of rehab.

choices.label: "Bench. Twenty minutes if we need it."

outcomes.text: She nods. "That I can sell."
You shrug and jog off. {physio.short} tells {boss.short} the truth anyway, and that you would not.

callbacks.line: "You do the rehab. Most don't."
"Not again. I'm telling him. You don't get to choose this time."
"Fit, are you? Properly fit? I'll be asking her, not you."

events.title: Chain 1 of 3: "Size nine?"
setup: Forty minutes to kick-off. {kid.name}'s sole has come clean off. He has one pair. He is trying to tape it and his hands are shaking.
He sees you looking. "You're a nine, aren't you?"

outcomes.text: He plays the game of his life in them. You play in your old pair, and your feet know it.

choices.label: "Tape's in the physio bag. Sort yourself out."

outcomes.text: He plays in a taped boot and comes off at half time with a blister the size of a coin.

callbacks.line: "Got my own boots now, if you were wondering."

events.title: Chain 2 of 3: He tries to give them back
setup: {kid.short} is waiting with your boots, cleaned better than you have ever cleaned them. "I get paid Friday. I'll get my own."

outcomes.text: He holds them like they might break.

choices.label: Sign them first. "For when you're famous."

outcomes.text: "When, not if?" "When." The lads saw. You are 'Mr Autograph' for a week.
Fair is fair. He looks at his own taped pair.

callbacks.line: "Still wearing them. Lucky ones."

events.title: Chain 3 of 3: Years later
setup: The tunnel. {kid.name} is a man now, and a captain. He is stood next to you in the line.
{if mem(kid,'you-signed-the-boots-when-not-if')}He lifts one foot. Your old boots. Your signature, nearly worn off. "When, not if. You said."{/if}
{if mem(kid,'you-gave-him-the-boots')}"I've still got them. They're in a glass case at my mum's."{/if}
{if mem(kid,'you-told-him-to-tape-it')}He does not look at you. "Tape's in the physio bag," he says, to nobody.{/if}

outcomes.text: After the match he tells the cameras the story. It is the most shared clip of the season.
He hugs you before the handshake line. The cameras catch it.
He marks you all game like it is personal. It is. He scores and runs past you to the away end.

callbacks.line: "Tape's in the physio bag, isn't it?"
"My mum's had three journalists round about those boots."

events.title: The long way round
setup: {mate.short} gets in. {if carTier>=3}He runs a hand along the dash. "This is a different life, mate."{/if}{if carTier<=2}He has to move a pile of kit off the seat to sit down.{/if}
You take the long way, past the ground and out along the coast road.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes of his awful playlist. He sings every word. It is the best you have felt all week.

choices.label: Ask how he is really doing.

outcomes.text: Quiet for a mile. Then it all comes out: his dad, the move, the nights. You just drive.
"Fine, mate. All good." He changes the subject to the weekend.

choices.label: Have a moan about the gaffer.

outcomes.text: You both do the gaffer's voice. He is better at it. You laugh until the lights change.
He tells a mate, who tells the assistant. It reaches the gaffer by Monday.

callbacks.line: "Cheers for the other day. In the car. I needed that."
"Enjoy your drive, did you? Walls have ears."
"Put my playlist on next time. You know you want to."

events.title: Blue lights
setup: {mate.short} dares you to open it up on the bypass. You do. Blue lights in the mirror a mile later.
The officer leans in, then does a double take. "Well, well."

outcomes.text: A fine and three points. The officer shakes your hand anyway.
He does. He wants a selfie for his son. You are let off with a warning.
He does. So does the paper by Tuesday: 'DO YOU KNOW WHO I AM?'

choices.label: Ask him to say he was driving.

outcomes.text: He takes the points for you. He does not say a word all the way home.
"Mate. No." The officer heard all of it. Double the fine.

callbacks.line: "Six points, mate. Six. You owe me."
"Still can't believe that copper wanted a selfie."

events.title: The whip-round
setup: The squad group chat: "Whip-round for {mate.short}'s birthday. Drop it in the kit room by Friday. No excuses."
Eleven people have already sent a thumbs up.

outcomes.text: He opens the card in the canteen and reads every name out.
Somebody screenshots it. You are 'Card at Home' for a month.

choices.label: Sort him a proper night out.

outcomes.text: A table, his family, a cake shaped like a boot. He makes a speech and cries.

callbacks.line: "Got your card today, have you?"
"Best birthday I've had since I was a kid. Cheers for that."

events.title: Boots in the ice bath
setup: {joker.short} has frozen {victim.short}'s new boots into a block in the ice bath. The whole room is waiting for him to walk in.
{joker.short} hands you his phone. "You film it."

outcomes.text: {victim.short} walks in, sees it, and laughs a second too late.

choices.label: Get the boots out before he arrives.

outcomes.text: {joker.short} calls you a killjoy. {victim.short} never knows how close it was, until somebody tells him.
Three million views. The gaffer has a word about 'the dressing room staying in the dressing room'.

callbacks.line: "Still got that video up, have you?"
"Heard about the boots. You didn't have to do that. Thanks."

events.title: A call at midnight
events.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.name}, at ten to midnight. He is outside somewhere; you can hear traffic.
"I'm in a hole, mate. Betting. I owe the wrong people about two weeks of what you earn. I wouldn't ask if there was anyone else."

outcomes.text: The money is in his account before he has finished saying thank you.

choices.label: "Ring the club welfare officer. Tonight. I'll come with you."

outcomes.text: He goes. It takes a long time, but he goes.
"I asked for money, not a lecture." He hangs up.
Silence. Then the line goes.
You say nothing for too long. "Forget it. Forget I rang." The line goes dead.

callbacks.line: "I've not had a bet in ten weeks. Thought you should know."
He answers, but he does not look up from his phone.

events.title: The loan
setup: {mate.short} sits down opposite you with two coffees. "About the money."

outcomes.text: He slides an envelope over. Every penny, and a bit more. "Interest."
"Not yet. Soon. I swear." You both know it is not soon.

choices.label: "Forget it. Just stay out of the bookies."

outcomes.text: He looks at the table for a long time. The money is gone; he is not.

callbacks.line: He is the first to stand up for you. "He's helped more people in here than you know."
"I know, I know. I'm sorting it."

events.title: The towel over his head
events.speaker: mate
setup: We won. {mate.short} played ten minutes. He plays where you play.
He is sat in the corner with a towel over his head while everyone else sings.

choices.label: Sit with him for a bit.

outcomes.text: Neither of you says much. You miss the singing. When you get up he says "cheers" to the floor.
The towel comes off. The look stays with you.
Probably what he wanted. Probably.
He does not look up. But he nods.

callbacks.line: "Train harder, you said. I did."
"Cheers for the other night. In the corner."

events.title: Thirty years at the club
setup: {kitman.name} has been at the club thirty years. He asks, a bit embarrassed, for a signed shirt for his grandson's hospital ward.

choices.label: Sign ten. Take them in yourself.

outcomes.text: The nurses line the corridor. His grandson will not let go of your hand.
"Lovely. Ta." He folds it like it is made of glass.
"Course." The lads heard. The dressing room goes a bit cold on you.

callbacks.line: "The ward's still got your shirts on the wall."
Your boots are not on your peg. He finds them, slowly.

events.title: Mum's birthday
setup: Dad, quietly: "It's your mum's birthday Sunday. You're away Saturday. Just so you know."

outcomes.text: She rings you from the hotel balcony in a dressing gown. Dad is in the background, pretending not to be pleased.

choices.label: Flowers, and a video call from the team bus.

outcomes.text: Half the squad shout happy birthday into your phone. She loves it.
Dad texts at nine on Sunday night: "She waited up."

callbacks.line: "Don't worry, love. I know you're busy."
"I'm still showing everyone the photos from that weekend."

events.title: Ten per cent
events.speaker: agent
setup: Your accountant, by text: "Your boot deal paid ten per cent more than {agent.short} told you. He kept the difference. Three seasons of it."

outcomes.text: He goes white, then pays it back by Friday. "A misunderstanding."
He denies it, then shouts, then hangs up. Your next deal will be harder to get.
You check every line of the next contract yourself. He notices.

choices.label: Sack him, and tell the papers why.

outcomes.text: It is a big story for two days. People who run football like a player who reads his contracts.

choices.label: Ask him nicely if there is a mistake.

outcomes.text: He apologises for 'an admin error' and pays half of it back.
"No mistake, kid. That's the fee." He sounds amused.

callbacks.line: "I've been straight with you since. Every penny."
He now works for the other side of the table.

events.title: The car park
events.speaker: stranger
setup: After the game, in the car park. A man in a quilted jacket walks with you to your car like he knows you.
"Yellow card before the twentieth minute on Saturday. Five weeks of your wages, cash. Nobody gets hurt."

outcomes.text: You get booked in the twelfth minute. Nobody says a word. The money is in a shoebox under your bed.
The betting people have been watching him for months. Your name is in their file. The club suspends you while it is looked at.

choices.label: Walk away. Report it to the club.

outcomes.text: The integrity people take a statement. The gaffer shakes your hand in front of the staff.
He watches you drive off. You check the mirror for a long time.

callbacks.line: "You've done it once. That makes the second time easy."
"I'll be watching your first twenty minutes. Every week."
The papers call you 'the one who said no'.

events.title: He knows where you park
events.speaker: stranger
setup: A withheld number, late.
{if mem(you,'took-the-yellow-card-money')}"Same again. A penalty given away this time. You know what happens if you say no now."{/if}
{if mem(you,'reported-the-fixer')}"You talked. I know where you park. I know where your mum parks."{/if}
{if mem(you,'said-nothing-to-the-fixer')}"Last chance. Ten weeks of your money for one bad pass."{/if}

choices.label: Go to the police. All of it.

outcomes.text: Statements, a panic alarm at your mum's, a court date in the spring. You are in the papers the right way round.
Ten weeks of money in a sports bag. You do not sleep.
It is the game the investigators were watching. It is over by Monday: suspended, every paper, every feed.
Nothing. Weeks of nothing. You still check the mirror.
Your car is burnt out on the drive at four in the morning. The insurance will not touch it.
You say nothing. He breathes down the line for a long time, then laughs and hangs up. You do not sleep.

callbacks.line: He is in court in the spring. Your name is in the paper, the right way round.
"Heard about your car. Anything you need, mate."

events.title: The recovery guy
events.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.short} has a 'recovery guy'. Little white pills in a plain tub. "Nothing on the list. They don't test for it. Your legs will thank you."
Your legs feel like concrete.

outcomes.text: You fly for a fortnight. Nobody asks. You keep the tub in your wash bag.
A random test, the Monday after. The sample does not come back clean.
He shrugs. "Your legs." You notice he does not offer twice.

choices.label: Tell the physio what he is handing round.

outcomes.text: The tub goes off to a lab. He is fined and dropped. He knows exactly who.
You leave the tub where it is and pull your boots on. {mate.short} shrugs and pockets it.

callbacks.line: "Didn't have you down as a grass."
"Your bloods came back odd. Anything you want to tell me?"

events.title: A letter from the ward
setup: The club forwards a letter. A boy on the children's ward, your shirt on the wall behind his bed. His operation is on Friday.
"Please could you say good luck. You are my best player."

outcomes.text: Two hours on the ward. {mate.short} does magic tricks, badly. The boy's mum films everything.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt and a note.

outcomes.text: His mum posts a photo of him holding it. It does well.
Somebody posts the letter with 'no reply'. It does better than the shirt would have.

callbacks.line: "Think about that kid a lot, you know. Hope he's all right."
Somebody has dug out the old letter again.

events.title: Young lads carry the kit
setup: First week. {vet.name} drops a net of twenty balls and a sack of bibs at your feet.
"Young lads carry the kit. Always have. Off you go."

outcomes.text: You carry them out and back every day that week. Nobody says thanks. {vet.short} nods once on Friday.
A couple of the lads laugh. {vet.short} doesn't.
He stares, then grins. "Cheeky. I like that." He carries them himself.

choices.label: Carry them, and his boot bag too.

outcomes.text: "Keen. Too keen." The lads call you his butler for a month.

callbacks.line: "Look who it is. Too good to carry a bag."
"Best bag man I ever had, you."
You remember the weight of that net of balls.

events.title: The first proper wage
setup: Mum rings. "Your first proper wage went in today, didn't it? I can hear it in your voice."
"What are you going to do with it, love?"

choices.label: "Pay off your catalogue. All of it."

outcomes.text: Silence. Then crying. Then Dad on the line: "What have you said to her?"
"Good lad. Your dad never saved a penny in his life."
"A watch. You've got a phone, love. It tells the time."

callbacks.line: "I kept the last statement. Zero. It's in a frame."
"How's the watch, love? Still telling the time?"

events.title: Somebody sent it to the gaffer
setup: The squad chat. Your joke about the gaffer's new hair, sent at 1 a.m.
Now {boss.short} has a screenshot of it. Somebody sent it. {leak.short} has gone very quiet.

outcomes.text: He lets you squirm for a full minute. "It is a bit much, the hair." The lads think you grovelled.
He sends one back. Phew.
He doesn't. You're on the bench on Saturday.
{leak.short} swears it wasn't him. Half the room believes him.

callbacks.line: "Want to check my phone again?"
"You came and said it to my face. About the hair. I respected that."

events.title: A hundred balls in the dark
setup: Everyone has gone in. {kitman.name} is still out there with a bag of balls and a flask.
"Bad one Saturday. Want me to feed you a hundred? I've got nowhere to be."

outcomes.text: It's dark when you finish. He tells the gaffer in the morning, loud enough for you to hear.
"Fair enough." He kicks the balls back in one by one, on his own.

choices.label: Do the hundred, then buy him a pint.

outcomes.text: He tells you about the 1998 cup run. Twice. You'd hear it a third time.

callbacks.line: "A hundred balls in the dark. Still the cleanest I've seen you hit them."
"Not too tired to sign it, I hope."

events.title: "Where does this end for you?"
setup: Your first goal worth talking about. {hack.name} of the {hack.outlet} wants five minutes for Sunday's paper.
"So, {you.short}. Where does this end for you?"

choices.label: "Next game. That's as far as I look."

outcomes.text: The piece is called 'Old Head on Young Shoulders'. The gaffer cuts it out.

choices.label: "I'll play for my country inside two years."

outcomes.text: Back page, big photo. The gaffer reads it out at breakfast in a silly voice.

choices.label: "Ask my mum. She drove me to every session."

outcomes.text: Your mum buys forty copies. The piece is mostly about her.

callbacks.line: "Inside two years, you said. That clip is still out there."
His reports call you 'the lad whose mum drove him'.

events.title: Still growing
setup: Both knees ache under the kneecap. {physio.name} presses, and you wince.
"You're still growing. Common at your age. Rest it or strap it. {boss.short} wants you Saturday."

outcomes.text: A week of ice and boredom. Then they feel like knees again.
It holds. You ice it for an hour after.
It flares. You limp off at half-time.

choices.label: "Give me the stretches. Every morning. I'll do them."

outcomes.text: She prints a sheet. You do every one, every morning. She notices.

callbacks.line: "You did the knee stretches as a kid. Do these."
"Strap it and play, is it? Like when you were a boy?"

events.title: BAMBI
setup: You fell over the ball on Saturday. Clean over it.
The club's own account has posted it, slowed down, with music. {joker.short} has commented 'BAMBI'. Twenty thousand likes.

outcomes.text: The fans love it. The gaffer hates it. The name sticks for good.

choices.label: Ask the club to take it down.

outcomes.text: It comes down. Screenshots don't.

choices.label: Find a clip of {joker.short} and post that.

outcomes.text: His own air shot from years ago. The lads crown you.
It isn't funny. He's hurt. The likes stop.

callbacks.line: "Morning, Bambi."
"Careful what you say. He'll get the club to delete you."

events.title: Free boots and a bit of money
setup: {agent.short} texts: "Stridewell want you in their boots. Small firm. Free pairs and a bit of money."
"Or we wait for a bigger name. Might take a year. Might never come."

outcomes.text: Six pairs in a box by Friday. They smell of glue and money.
Five weeks later a bigger name rings. Double the money.
Nobody rings. Stridewell sign a lad from the academy instead.

choices.label: "Dad bought my first boots. I'm asking him."

outcomes.text: Dad reads it with his glasses on his head. "Take it. And get a pair for your brother."

callbacks.line: "Last time you made me wait for a bigger boot. Don't do it twice."
"I've still got the first boots I bought you. Size four."

events.title: Forty quid each
setup: {bro.short} rings, too cheerful.
"Those comp tickets you give me. I've been, er, passing them on. Forty quid each. The club's asking questions. Got my back?"

choices.label: "Stop. Today. I'll tell them it was a mix-up."

outcomes.text: "Fine. Killjoy." He stops. Mostly.

choices.label: "Say they were mine to give. Carry on."

outcomes.text: Nothing comes of it. He buys you a takeaway with the profits.
The club find out. Your comps are stopped and you're fined.
He hangs up. Mum rings ten minutes later to ask what you've done.

callbacks.line: "Can I have a ticket? Joking. I know the rule."
"Still not touting. Ask anyone."

events.title: 2 a.m., a number you don't know
setup: 2 a.m. A number you don't know. It's {bro.short}, from a police station.
"Fight outside a club. Not my fault. Don't tell Mum. I need a solicitor and I need one now."

choices.label: Pay for a solicitor. Tell nobody.

outcomes.text: He's out by breakfast. No charge. He hugs you in the car park for too long.
He's out by breakfast. So is the story: 'STAR'S BROTHER IN BRAWL'.
Mum is there before you are, in her dressing gown. He doesn't speak to you for a fortnight.
He gets the duty solicitor. He doesn't ring you for a month.

callbacks.line: "Don't worry. I won't need a solicitor this time."
"I owe you for that night. I'll always owe you."

events.title: "Explain."
setup: {boss.short} texts you a photo: you and {mate.short} in a club at 1 a.m. on a Thursday. Match on Saturday.
One word under it: "Explain."

outcomes.text: A week's fine. "At least you didn't lie to me. Most do."
He lets it go. You think.
The photo has the date on it. He fines you, and drops you.
{mate.short} gets the fine. He finds out who said it by lunch.

callbacks.line: "Is that an old photo too?"
"Don't worry, I'll take the blame. I always do."
"You owned it once. Don't make me ask twice."

events.title: He owes people
setup: Halfway down the bypass {mate.short} goes quiet. Then he says it.
"I've been betting. On our games. Small stuff. Then not small. I owe people."

outcomes.text: He cries a bit. You pull into a lay-by till he's done. The call takes an hour.
You transfer it from the lay-by. He swears it's the last time.

choices.label: Drive straight to the training ground. Tell the gaffer.

outcomes.text: Betting on football is a ban. He knows you knew that. He doesn't look at you in the car.

callbacks.line: "Eleven weeks clean. Thought you'd want to know."
He stops looking for you in tight spots.

events.title: Two men by his car
setup: {mate.short} rings from the training car park. His voice is wrong.
"Two blokes by my car. It wasn't the last time. It's more now. Three weeks of your money. Please."

outcomes.text: They take the bag and nod at you like you work for them now.

choices.label: Ring the police, then the club.

outcomes.text: The men are gone before the police come. {mate.short} is suspended while the club looks into his betting.

choices.label: Drive over and get him out of there.

outcomes.text: You pull up, he jumps in, you go. They write down your number plate.
One of them puts a brick through your windscreen. On camera.

callbacks.line: He has paid you back forty quid. He says the rest is coming.
"You came. Nobody else would have."

events.title: "Tonight only"
setup: {agent.name} rings. Smooth voice. "I've watched you since the academy. Four years, ten per cent, and I make you rich."
"Sign tonight and there's a little welcome bonus. Tonight only."

outcomes.text: The bonus lands at midnight. Dad finds out at breakfast. He puts his toast down.
Dad finds a line about your image rights. {agent.short} sighs and takes it out.

choices.label: Pay a lawyer to read it.

outcomes.text: Three pages of changes. He signs them all. "You'll be hard work," he laughs.

callbacks.line: He reads every clause twice now. He knows you will.
"Still want me reading the small print, son?"

events.title: Perfectly legal. Mostly.
setup: {agent.short}: "Your image rights. We put them in a company overseas. Perfectly legal. Mostly."
"Saves you a fortune in tax. Everyone does it."

outcomes.text: Papers signed in a car park. Nothing happens.
Papers signed in a car park. Nothing happens. Yet.

choices.label: "Pay the tax. I'm not that player."

outcomes.text: "Your money, your funeral." He sounds like he means the funeral.
Your accountant goes white. "Do not sign that. Ever."

callbacks.line: "Want to run this one past your accountant as well?"
A reporter asks about 'tax arrangements'. You say nothing, very quickly.

events.title: A letter from the taxman
setup: A letter from the taxman. Then a text from {hack.name}: "Comment on your overseas company before we print?"
{agent.short} isn't answering.

choices.label: Pay it all back, and the fine.

outcomes.text: It hurts. The story runs small, on page nineteen.
You win on a technicality. Nobody thinks you were innocent.
You lose. Front page: 'TAX DODGE STAR'.
You pay, and you name him. He loses half his clients by Christmas.

callbacks.line: He asks for 2% more on every deal. "Danger money."
"No comment, is it? Like the tax?"

events.title: The heat map
setup: {hack.name} in the {hack.outlet}: "{you.short} jogged for ninety minutes. A luxury this club cannot afford."
He has printed the heat map. It is not a kind heat map.

choices.label: Post your sprint numbers under it.

outcomes.text: You ran further than anyone on the pitch. He corrects it, through his teeth.
Your numbers are worse than his. The replies are brutal.

choices.label: Say nothing. Run more on Saturday.

outcomes.text: Extra sprints all week. Your legs answer for you.

choices.label: Invite him to watch you train.

outcomes.text: He stays all morning and writes about the running nobody sees. The gaffer hates press at training.

callbacks.line: His pieces mention 'the extra running nobody sees'.
"Brought your sprint numbers today?"

events.title: When you were fourteen
setup: The {hack.outlet} has found your posts from when you were fourteen. You called this club 'a pub team with a car park'.
Forty thousand shares. {boss.short} wants a word.

outcomes.text: Ninety seconds, no script. Most fans accept it. Some never will.

choices.label: "I was fourteen. I also had a fringe."

outcomes.text: It lands. Fans post photos of their own fringes.
It doesn't land. 'Arrogant' is the word.
Nobody can prove otherwise. {hack.short} keeps digging.
{hack.short} proves otherwise. Second story, bigger than the first.

callbacks.line: "Been hacked again lately?"
"How's the fringe?"

events.title: The vote
setup: {boss.short} wants the squad to vote for a vice-captain. It's you or {vet.name}.
{vet.short} catches you at the coffee machine. "Back me this once. Your time's coming."

outcomes.text: He wins it. He tells the room who swung it. The gaffer wanted you.
You win by two votes. {vet.short} shakes your hand. Barely.
You lose by two votes. Everyone knows you didn't back him.
You don't vote. Both sides notice.

callbacks.line: "You backed me when you didn't have to."
He passes to you. He doesn't look at you.

events.title: Full time, and a water bottle
setup: Full time. {other.short} throws a water bottle at {mate.short}: "Your man. Your goal." {mate.short} goes for him.
The room freezes. You're nearest.

outcomes.text: You take a shove and it's over. The gaffer never hears about it.
You take an elbow in the eye. It's in every photo on Monday.
Two against one. {other.short} backs off and doesn't forget it.
Both fined. Both know who shouted.

callbacks.line: "Saw the eye, by the way. Proper hero."
"Your mate not with you today?"

events.title: "He starts Saturday"
setup: {boss.short} calls you in. "{kid.short} starts Saturday. In your spot. He's {kid.age}. I need to see him."
Through the window, {kid.short} is pretending not to watch.

outcomes.text: You walk him through your runs all week. The papers say you've been replaced.
He thinks about it. "Prove it this week." You start.
"Decision's made." Door shut. The kid heard all of it.
He notices. Everyone notices.

callbacks.line: "You showed me how to play your position. I won't forget it."
"Going to skip the warm-down again?"

events.title: Six hours on your day off
setup: {agent.short}: "Brightwave shoot tomorrow. Your day off. Six hours. They pay well."
You were going to sleep till noon.

outcomes.text: Six hours of pretending to drink a drink you'd never drink.
They move it. Grudgingly.
They drop you from the campaign. {agent.short} loses his cut too.
Two hours. They get what they get.

callbacks.line: "They've asked if you'll actually turn up this time."
"Brightwave loved you. They asked for you by name."

events.title: $GOAL
setup: {agent.short}: "A crypto lot want you on their coin. $GOAL. Three posts. Six weeks' wages."
"Fans buy in. Everyone wins. Probably."

outcomes.text: Three posts. The coin jumps. Your replies are full of rocket faces.
"Somebody else will." Somebody else does.

choices.label: "Cash up front, and one post only."

outcomes.text: One post. The money is in your account before it's live.

callbacks.line: "You were right about the coin. Don't tell anyone I said so."
Someone in the crowd holds up a $GOAL sign. Upside down.

events.title: Down 96% overnight
setup: $GOAL has fallen 96% overnight. Fans are posting what they lost. One is a lad who put in his paper-round money.
{hack.outlet}: "{you.short}'S COIN CRASH".

choices.label: Pay the fans back. Your own money.

outcomes.text: It takes a month and a spreadsheet. The paper-round lad sends a photo of his new bike.
Deleted. Screenshots aren't.
True, and nobody cares. {agent.short} stops taking your calls.

callbacks.line: "Any coins to plug today?"
His paper calls you 'the one who paid them back'.

events.title: "Asking for my cousin"
setup: {mate.short}: "Quick one. You starting Saturday? And is the keeper's back still bad? Asking for my cousin."
Last time his cousin asked, he had a bet on.

outcomes.text: "Legend." Nothing else. You feel sick all Saturday.
The betting firm flags his cousin's bet. The club's integrity officer wants to see you both.
"Calm down, it's only a question." It wasn't.

choices.label: Screenshot it. Send it to the integrity officer.

outcomes.text: He's banned for six games. The dressing room knows exactly why.

callbacks.line: "Careful what you say near him. He screenshots."
"You've given a tip before. Don't pretend you haven't."

events.title: The integrity officer
setup: The integrity officer has a laptop with your text on it. {mate.short} is in the next room.
"Did you know why he was asking?"

outcomes.text: Six games and a fine. 'Honest,' they write. It still hurts.

choices.label: "No idea. I thought it was chat."

outcomes.text: They can't prove you knew. A warning. {mate.short} takes the ban alone.
His cousin's phone says otherwise. Eight games.
A short ban for you. A long one for him.

callbacks.line: "You and the truth. Strangers, aren't you?"
He has not said a word to you since the hearing.

events.title: The investor in the suite
setup: {agent.short} has set up a meeting: an overseas investor, a hotel suite, champagne at 3 p.m. He wants you as an 'ambassador'.
Then: "How would a player get round the betting rules? Hypothetically."

outcomes.text: He was real. Odd, but real. You leave with a deal.
Sunday, the {hack.outlet}: a hidden camera, your face, your words. 'STAR'S BETTING TIPS'.
On Sunday the {hack.outlet} stings someone else. There's a note on your car: "Clever lad."
You spot the camera in the lamp and film the man filming you. It's their story that dies.
One sentence too many, trying to be clever. It's in the paper.

callbacks.line: "No cameras today. Promise."
You check every lamp in every hotel room now.

events.title: The needle in the tunnel
setup: In the tunnel your ankle screams. {physio.name} has the needle ready. "Numbs it for ninety minutes. Then you pay for it."
{boss.short}, at the door: "Your call, son. I need you."

outcomes.text: You can't feel your foot. You play well anyway.
The ankle goes in the second half. You never felt it go.
He says nothing. He doesn't have to.

choices.label: No needle. Tape it and run.

outcomes.text: It holds. Ugly, but it holds.
Off at half-time, limping.

callbacks.line: "You've had the needle before. Your body keeps count."
"I asked you to play through it once. You didn't."

events.title: Dad in the away end
setup: A clip is everywhere: your dad, red in the face, squaring up to a fan who called you useless.
Stewards. A ban letter is coming. {boss.short} has seen it.

choices.label: Post: "He's my dad. He loves me. Back off."

outcomes.text: Thousands of dads share it. {boss.short} asks you to keep family off the internet.

choices.label: Ask him to stay home for a bit.

outcomes.text: "Right. Course." He watches the next six on the telly, alone.

choices.label: Get him a seat in the family box.

outcomes.text: Padded seats, free tea. He hates it. He likes the away end.

callbacks.line: "I'll watch it on the telly. Don't worry about me."
"Your post. I read it most days. Don't tell your mum."

events.title: The boiler's gone again
setup: Mum's boiler has gone again. She mentions it like it's nothing. It's never nothing.
{bro.short} texts while she's talking: "Buy her a house. You can. I can't."

outcomes.text: She says no four times. On the fifth she cries. The new kitchen has a window over the garden.
A new boiler by Thursday. {bro.short} sends a thumbs up. Just the thumb.
"Course, love. No rush." There's a rush.

callbacks.line: "I still walk round the new kitchen touching things."
"Is it next year yet, love?"

events.title: "I could be your agent"
setup: {bro.short}: "Why are you paying {agent.short} ten per cent? I could do it. I know you. I'd never rob you."
He has done a course. Online. Six weeks.

outcomes.text: {agent.short} takes the news in total silence, then hangs up. {bro.short} buys a suit.
"Right. Got it." He hangs up first.
{agent.short} agrees, through his teeth. You pay {bro.short}'s train fares. He takes notes in a new notebook.

callbacks.line: Your old agent sits across the table now. For the other club.
"How's your proper agent? The one who's not family?"

events.title: Two boot firms, one Monday
setup: {bro.short}: "Slight problem. I've signed you to two boot firms. Same week. Both want you on Monday."
One of them has lawyers. The other has bigger lawyers.

outcomes.text: He sorts it. Somehow. He's very proud of himself.
He doesn't. Both firms walk. You pay one of them off.
The suit goes back in the wardrobe. So does he, for a while.

choices.label: Pay the smaller firm off yourself. Say nothing.

outcomes.text: He never knows. He thinks he fixed it.

callbacks.line: Christmas is quiet. Your brother sits at the far end of the table.
"I've been reading contracts properly now. Both pages."

events.title: Junction nine
setup: {agent.short} rings as you drive: "Pull into the services at junction nine. A director from a big club is in the coffee place. Ten minutes."
Meeting a club behind your own club's back is against the rules. It happens every week.

outcomes.text: Ten minutes. He likes you. Very much. Nobody saw.
A fan films you shaking his hand. It's online by teatime.
"Your loss." He rings off. The services shrink in the mirror.

choices.label: Drive on, and tell the gaffer who's sniffing.

outcomes.text: He writes the director's name on a pad and underlines it twice.

callbacks.line: He asks if you've 'stopped for a coffee' lately.
"You told me about the services. I've not forgotten."

events.title: Three nights, midweek
setup: {mate.short}: "Getting married! Stag do. Three nights abroad, the week after next."
"It's midweek. The gaffer doesn't need to know."

outcomes.text: Three nights. You remember about half of it.
One night. You're on the first flight back, in sunglasses.
"Boring." He sends you forty photos from the trip anyway.

callbacks.line: "You missed a good one. Wedding's in June. Don't miss that."
"What happens on the stag. You know."

events.title: On a bar, nine days before the derby
setup: The {hack.outlet} has the stag photos: you and {mate.short} dancing on a bar, midweek, nine days before the derby.
{boss.short} has the paper on his desk.

outcomes.text: Two weeks' wages. {mate.short} tries to pay half. You don't let him.

choices.label: "It was his stag. I was looking after him."

outcomes.text: He gets the bigger fine. He reads why in the paper.
It works. Somehow.
The bar posted it themselves, with the date. Double fine.

callbacks.line: "Still owe you for the stag fine. Wedding drinks are on me."
"Any more old photos I should know about?"

events.title: Can I have your shirt?
setup: Your mascot today is a lad of eight with a home-made sign: '{you.short}, CAN I HAVE YOUR SHIRT?'
{mate.short} nudges you. "Go on. Make his year."

outcomes.text: You give it him at full time, soaking. He holds it like a trophy.

choices.label: Ruffle his hair. Stay locked in.

outcomes.text: He looks at the floor. You look at the pitch.

choices.label: Your warm-up top now. His sign for your wall.

outcomes.text: The kit man has to find you another top. The sign goes up in your hall.

callbacks.line: Years on, a young pro tells you he was that mascot. He still has the top.
"Saw the mascot thing. Soft lad."

events.title: After the miss
setup: Your phone after the miss: hundreds of messages. Some are vile. Some are about your family.
The club's head of security texts: "Want us to take these to the police?"

outcomes.text: Two arrests by the weekend. Other players start reporting theirs.
Quiet. You still know it's there.
Thousands back you. He deletes his account.
Your reply becomes the story, not his message.

callbacks.line: A reporter asks about the abuse case. You answer properly.
After every miss now, the trolls wait for a reply.

events.title: Window up, in the rain
setup: A clip online: you driving through the training gate past six kids in the rain holding shirts. Window up.
You didn't even see them. Nobody believes that. {boss.short} has seen it too.

choices.label: Go back to the gate tomorrow with signed shirts.

outcomes.text: An hour in the drizzle. Every shirt signed, every photo taken.
"Didn't see you, lads. Sorry." Half believe it.
It's one clip, then three, then a compilation.

callbacks.line: "Saw you out at the gate in the rain. Fair play."
Every time you drive in, someone films the window.

events.title: A number you don't know
setup: A number you don't know. "It's the national team coach. We've lost a player to injury. We want you this week."
{if mem(you,'promised-a-cap')}You said 'inside two years' in an interview once. Here it is.{/if}
Ten minutes later, {boss.short}: "Cup game next week. Tell them you've got a knock."

outcomes.text: Twelve minutes off the bench. Your dad is in the stand in a scarf he bought that morning.

choices.label: Tell them you've got a knock.

outcomes.text: They pick someone else. He scores.
A national team doctor checks. There's no knock. It leaks.

choices.label: Tell the coach the truth: your club won't let you.

outcomes.text: The coach rings your chairman. Your gaffer finds out who told.

callbacks.line: Dad has the cap in a frame in the hall.
"You did me a favour with the national team. I owe you one."

events.title: "Why won't he sing?"
setup: {hack.outlet}: a slow-motion clip of your closed mouth during the anthem. 'WHY WON'T HE SING?'
Dad rings. "You never could sing. Tell them that."

outcomes.text: You do. Badly. It's the most-liked clip of your career.

choices.label: "My dad says I can't sing. He's right."

outcomes.text: Dad posts a video of you at eight, singing terribly. You win the week.
Some think you're mocking the anthem. The row gets bigger.
Half the country loves it. The other half has a column.

callbacks.line: "Singing yet?"
"I've got more videos. Don't push me."

events.title: Where do you want them?
setup: {kid.name}, {kid.age}, has picked up the ball net and the bibs without being told.
{if mem(you,'carried-the-bags-as-a-kid')}You carried that same net once. Your arms remember.{/if}{if mem(you,'refused-the-bags')}You refused that net once. The lads still tell it.{/if}
"Where do you want them, {you.short}?"

choices.label: "Cones by the goal. Balls in the middle."

outcomes.text: He does it perfectly. Every day. Nobody says thanks. You know how that feels.

choices.label: Take half of it off him.

outcomes.text: A couple of the old heads tut: tradition. The kid can't stop grinning.
He does it. He doesn't smile while he does it.

callbacks.line: "You carried the net with me, my first week. Remember?"
"Want me to carry your coffee too?"

events.title: Tuesdays with the under-18s
setup: {boss.short}: "Start your badges. Take the under-18s on Tuesdays. Lads like {kid.short} need someone like you."
It means a day of your week, every week.

outcomes.text: Your first session is a shambles. Your second is better. {kid.short} stays behind to ask questions.
"Not yet becomes never quicker than you think."
He laughs. "Fine. Cheeky."
"Don't bargain with me. Not about that."

callbacks.line: The club offers you the under-18s the day you retire.
"Tuesdays with you made me. Honestly."

events.title: "Mind out, granddad"
setup: {kid.short}, {kid.age}, loud enough for the whole pitch: "Mind out, granddad's on the ball."
The lads laugh. Then they look at you to see what happens.

outcomes.text: You win by a yard. You can't breathe for a minute. Worth it.
He wins by five yards and waves on the way back.

choices.label: "Granddad's got more medals than you've got followers."

outcomes.text: The lads howl. So does he.

choices.label: Next drill, go through him. Fair, but hard.

outcomes.text: He gets up quieter. A lot quieter.
You catch him wrong. He's off to the physio. The gaffer goes mad.

callbacks.line: "Rematch? When you've had a lie down."
"Going to kick me again, granddad?"

events.title: A cut for life
setup: {agent.short}: "My mate's opening steak restaurants. Three sites. Footballers love it. You put in, you get a cut for life."
Dad, when you tell him: "Your grandad lost the house on a 'cut for life'."

outcomes.text: Packed every night. The cheques start arriving.
Two sites shut within a year. The third is a vape shop now. The money is gone.
It does fine. You get a free steak whenever you like.
Gone. Smaller hole, same hole.
{agent.short} calls you boring. Dad calls you sensible, which from him is a lot.

callbacks.line: "Steak, is it? No thanks."
"You listened about the money. Your grandad never did."

events.title: A season on camera
setup: {agent.short}: "A streaming firm want a fly-on-the-wall season on you. Home, training, the car. Big money."
{boss.short} hears about it before you've replied.

outcomes.text: Cameras in the dressing room by Monday. The lads start wearing their good trainers.

choices.label: "Home and the car. Not the dressing room."

outcomes.text: Less money. Less fuss. The car turns out to be the dangerous bit.
"They'll make one about someone else, then." They do.

callbacks.line: "Is that thing filming? Turn it off."
"The other lad's film did well, by the way."

events.title: Episode four
setup: Episode four drops. The car camera caught you ranting about {mate.short}: "He can't pass, he can't run, he can't anything."
{mate.short} has watched it. So has everyone.

choices.label: Find him. Apologise to his face.

outcomes.text: He lets you finish. "You meant it, though." Then he shakes your hand.
Fans love the honesty. The dressing room doesn't.
The firm stays quiet. Most believe you.
The firm posts the full clip. It's worse.

callbacks.line: He passes to you. Barely.
"Saw episode five. You were nice about me. Weird."

events.title: Ten years
setup: A letter from the chairman: a testimonial match in the summer. Old team-mates, a full stadium, and the gate money is yours.
Dad: "All those years at one club. Your grandad would have cried."

choices.label: All of it to the children's hospital.

outcomes.text: Thirty thousand come. Every penny goes to the ward.

choices.label: Keep the gate. You've earned it.

outcomes.text: A full house and a big cheque. A few banners ask where the money is going.

choices.label: Half to the hospital. Half for the family.

outcomes.text: Dad does the half-time draw. He's terrible at it. Everyone loves him.

callbacks.line: The hospital names a ward after you the week you retire.
"How's the testimonial money? All spent?"

events.title: "Packing it in"
setup: {old.short} rings. "Packing it in, mate. Knees have gone. Leaving do on Thursday."
"You were one of the good ones. Would mean a lot."

outcomes.text: You drive two hours. He makes a speech. Your name is in it, twice.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt and a long message.

outcomes.text: He reads your message out at the do. Someone films it.
"Course. Course. Good luck Saturday."

callbacks.line: "You came to my do. Half the lads didn't."
He coaches a youth side now. He mentions every old team-mate but you.

events.title: The scan
setup: {physio.name} turns the screen towards you. "Not much cartilage left in that knee. Not much at all."
"We manage your minutes, or we inject it and pretend."

outcomes.text: Off at sixty, every week. The crowd claps you off. You hate it, and it works.
Feels new. For now.
It flares within a month. Worse than before.

choices.label: "Don't tell the gaffer how bad it is."

outcomes.text: She says nothing to him. She says a lot to you, with her face.

callbacks.line: "Sixty minutes. You stuck to it. The knee thanks you."
At your leaving do she tells you she nearly quit over that scan.

events.title: Dad's had a turn
setup: Mum, very calm, which is worse: "Your dad's had a turn. His heart. He's in. He's asking for you, then saying don't come."
Training is at nine. There's a match on Saturday.

outcomes.text: You sit by the bed in your training kit all night. He pretends to be annoyed you came.

choices.label: Pay for the best private care. Ring every night.

outcomes.text: A private room, the best man in the country. Mum says thank you. She wanted you, not the room.
He's fine, in the end. Mum doesn't ring you for a while.

callbacks.line: "You came in your training kit. I won't forget that."
"He asked for you, you know. Even after he said not to."

lines: "That's more like it. Did you see the gaffer's face at the end?"
"Don't read the papers this week. Trust me."
"The missus says you have to come round for tea. She's not asking."
He answers in one word. Then the headphones go back in.
"How did you deal with it? Your first season, I mean?"
"Look after your knees. Nobody tells you that."
"Still learning where everything is. Where do you sit in the canteen?"
"Saw the motor. What does that do, nought to sixty?"
"How's the horse? Is it actually fast or just good-looking?"
"Skipper. What's the gaffer really like with you?"
"My little brother has your poster up. Don't let it go to your head."
"One of us is starting Saturday. No hard feelings, whatever happens."
